topic.subject: science
topic.title: Fun with magnets
topic.scope: magnetic and non-magnetic materials, poles, attraction and repulsion, compass, storing magnets

misconceptions.statement: All shiny metal objects are magnetic.
misconceptions.why: Students often associate the metallic luster of objects like coins or aluminum foil with the properties of iron.
misconceptions.fix: Only specific materials like iron, nickel, and cobalt are attracted to magnets; many other metals are not.

probe.question: Will a magnet attract a shiny aluminum spoon?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because it is made of metal.

misconceptions.why: Students often see magnets picking up various things in toys and assume the attraction is universal.
misconceptions.fix: Magnets only attract materials that have magnetic properties; they do not affect plastic, wood, or glass.

probe.question: Will a magnet pick up a plastic pen?

misconceptions.statement: The middle of a magnet is the strongest part.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the physical center of the object with the location of the magnetic force.
misconceptions.fix: The magnetic force is concentrated at the two ends, called poles, and is weakest in the middle.

probe.question: Where will the most iron filings stick to a bar magnet?
probe.wrong_answer: In the middle of the magnet.

misconceptions.why: Students often confuse the terminology of 'opposite' with 'repulsion' due to linguistic similarity.
misconceptions.fix: Like poles repel each other, while opposite poles attract each other.

probe.question: What happens when you bring a North pole near a South pole?

misconceptions.statement: The compass needle points North because it is attracted to the North Pole of the Earth.
misconceptions.why: Students assume the 'North' pole of the magnet is attracted to the 'North' pole of the Earth.
misconceptions.fix: The North pole of the compass needle is attracted to the Earth's magnetic South pole, which is located near the geographic North.

probe.question: Why does the compass needle point North?
probe.wrong_answer: Because the North pole of the magnet likes the North pole of the Earth.
